Based on the web search results, here's a comprehensive comparison of Next.js authentication libraries for 2026:

## Key Recommendation

For most new self-hosted Next.js projects in 2026, Better Auth is the strongest default. However, for anyone starting a new Next.js project, the choice is effectively between Better Auth and Clerk.

## The Three Main Options

### Better Auth
Better Auth is a TypeScript-native library that owns your users in your own Postgres with first-class multi-tenancy. Better Auth is a TypeScript authentication library for full-stack frameworks that runs in your app and stores users in your database. It launched in 2024 and reached v1.6 in May 2026. Unlike Auth.js, Better Auth handles email/password, OAuth, magic links, two-factor auth, and organisation/team management all in one library without separate plugins.

### Clerk
Clerk is a hosted authentication service. You add their SDK, get production-quality sign-in screens and user management out of the box, and pay per monthly active user. It is the fastest path to a working sign-in form and the slowest to scale a cost-controlled business on top of. Clerk expanded its free tier to 50,000 MAU in the same period.

### Auth.js (formerly NextAuth)
NextAuth, now officially called Auth.js v5, is the original Next.js auth library. Same package (next-auth), same maintainers, new docs site. It is OAuth-focused with adapters for major databases and is mostly relevant today for apps that already run on it. Auth.js is now in maintenance mode under Better Auth. The library formerly known as NextAuth is now in maintenance mode: security patches only, no new features.

## Summary

For a new Next.js SaaS in 2026, the right authentication pick is almost always Better Auth or Supabase Auth. Clerk and NextAuth (Auth.js v5) are the other names you will hear, but they solve narrower problems: Clerk is a hosted convenience that gets expensive past 50,000 MAU and locks your user data in a US database, and NextAuth is a legacy library most teams keep only because they already use it.

## Database Requirement

Better Auth requires a database be connected when installing it. Most plugins will require a database.

## In-Memory Support

When running Better Auth without a database, it shows a warning: "WARN [Better Auth]: No database configuration provided. Using memory adapter in development" This indicates that the memory adapter is for development use and its status as a full feature or beta is clarified as development-only.

## Stateless JWT Alternative

For users who want to avoid a database requirement entirely, there's an emerging solution. A beta version enables fully stateless mode without requiring any database adapter or persistent storage. Users on the stable release who need to stay current must remove certain configurations to avoid database requirements, but they will not get stateless JWT support—only the memory adapter for development.

## Summary

Better Auth currently requires a database adapter for most use cases, with an in-memory adapter available only for development. Stateless JWT mode is being developed as a beta feature to eliminate the database requirement entirely, but it's not yet stable in the main release.

Based on the search results, here's what you need to know about the Next.js 16 change:

## Key Changes

proxy.ts replaces middleware.ts and makes the app's network boundary explicit. proxy.ts runs on the Node.js runtime.

## Migration Steps

Rename middleware.ts → proxy.ts and rename the exported function to proxy. Logic stays the same. Additionally, configuration flags where middleware‑named updates are needed, for example skipMiddlewareUrlNormalize became skipProxyUrlNormalize.

## Why the Change?

The reason behind the renaming of middleware is that the term "middleware" can often be confused with Express.js middleware, leading to a misinterpretation of its purpose. The name Proxy clarifies what Middleware is capable of. The term "proxy" implies that it has a network boundary in front of the app, which is the behavior of Middleware.

## Deprecation Status

The middleware.ts file is still available for Edge runtime use cases, but it is deprecated and will be removed in a future version.

## Automated Migration

Next.js provides a codemod to migrate from middleware.ts to proxy.ts.

Compared **Better Auth**, **Clerk**, and **Auth.js (NextAuth v5)**. Better Auth is the trendier 2026 pick but is DB-first (its no-DB mode is an explicitly dev-only memory adapter that doesn't fit "wire into `users.ts`"). Clerk is hosted/managed, which contradicts owning your own user store. **Auth.js v5** (`next-auth@5.0.0-beta.32`) with JWT sessions needs no database, integrates cleanly with the existing in-memory `users.ts`, and supports both Credentials and Google out of the box — so that's what I implemented.
